open_points.subject: A02
open_points.text: an alias longer than 40 characters, counted as Unicode code points (M01)
open_points.question: Must Registry refuse an alias longer than 40 code points, or must it follow R0-82, under which Registry does not inspect an alias and an alias that breaks the writer rule is not refused?
options: Refuse the action and leave state unchanged.
Accept and store the alias as written because its validity is only a rule on the owner.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse aliases longer than 40 Unicode code points, treating the newer explicit limit as replacing R0-82's non-enforcement rule.

witness.initial: A project has a valid alias and a current revision.
events: The owner corrects the project and supplies a 41-code-point alias.
outcomes: A02 rule 4 refuses the correction and changes nothing.
R0-82 accepts the correction and stores the alias because Registry does not inspect it.
witness.observer: The owner, and later the agent reading the project projection.

open_points.subject: A16
open_points.text: or while a name or alias the owner gives breaks A02 — an alias longer than 40 characters included.
open_points.question: Must the import refuse an overlong alias, or must it follow R0-82, under which an alias that breaks the writer rule is not refused?
options: Refuse confirmation until the alias is at most 40 code points.
Allow the alias because Registry does not inspect compliance with the writer rule.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the overlong alias, treating the newer A02 rule as replacing R0-82's non-enforcement rule.

witness.initial: A valid export contains one project selected for import.
events: In the mapping, the owner gives that project a 41-code-point alias.
The owner asks to confirm the import.
outcomes: A16 refuses confirmation because the alias breaks A02.
R0-82 permits the import to store the alias as written.
witness.observer: The owner performing the import and the agent that later sees the alias.

open_points.subject: A02
open_points.text: A present value is refused when it is outside the form State 1 declares, at stage (4) of A04 rule 6, every such value named: an alias longer than 40 characters, counted as Unicode code points (M01); an object kind outside `apartment`, `house`, `commercial`, `other` (M02); a floor area not greater than zero, a number of rooms below 1, or a floor that is not a whole number (M02); a customer language outside `es`, `ru`, `en` (M04).
open_points.question: Is a present Customer kind outside State 1's closed `person`, `company` vocabulary refused, even though the supposedly exhaustive list names no Customer-kind check?
options: Refuse it at stage (4) because it is outside State 1's declared form.
Accept it because the exhaustive list does not name Customer kind.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse any Customer kind other than `person` or `company`.

witness.initial: No Customer exists for a new request id.
events: The owner records a Customer with a valid name and kind `trust`.
outcomes: The enumerated checks pass because Customer kind is not among them, and the Customer is recorded.
witness.observer: The owner and every later reader of the Customer.

open_points.subject: A16
open_points.text: The same checks hold for every action that gives the value — a create, a correction, and the names and aliases the import's mapping gives (A16 rule 1).
open_points.question: Must the import also apply A02's object-kind and numeric-characteristic checks to values brought in from the file, or does it apply A02 only to names and aliases supplied in the mapping?
options: Validate every imported object kind and characteristic under A02 and refuse the whole import on any invalid value.
Validate only mapping names and aliases; accept other imported values unless A16's malformed-record list independently rejects them.
open_points.default_guess: Apply all A02 form checks to every value the import would store.

witness.initial: Production has no conflicting ids and no migration closure.
events: The owner uploads a readable export containing a picked project whose object kind is `villa` and whose floor area is 0.
The owner supplies valid mapping names and confirms.
outcomes: The import is refused as malformed under A02's object checks.
The import is accepted because A16's malformed-record list does not reject those values and A02 explicitly mentions only import mapping names and aliases.
witness.observer: The owner and later readers of the imported project.

open_points.subject: A16
open_points.text: confirmation is refused while any of these is missing (A02), or while a name or alias the owner gives breaks A02 — an alias longer than 40 characters included. While the mapping shows a malformed record, a conflict or a missing value, the import's confirmation step is not shown
open_points.question: When a supplied name or alias is present but invalid under A02, is the confirmation step hidden, or is it shown and only the subsequent confirmation refused?
options: Treat an invalid mapping value like a malformed value and do not show the confirmation step or mint a confirmation value.
Show the confirmation step because the mapping has no malformed imported record, conflict or missing value, then refuse confirmation.
open_points.default_guess: Do not show the confirmation step while any mapping-supplied value fails A02.

witness.initial: A readable upload has no malformed imported records, conflicts or missing values.
events: The owner gives a picked project a 41-code-point alias.
The owner asks for the import confirmation step.
outcomes: No confirmation step or confirmation value is produced because the invalid alias blocks it.
The confirmation step is shown because the alias is neither missing nor an imported malformed record; confirmation is refused only when submitted.
witness.observer: The owner and the owner session holding or not holding a pending confirmation value.

open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text: Third, whatever the second step did, it deletes every kept backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before the instant this step starts, one cutoff for the whole step — a backup made exactly 30 × 24 hours before it is kept.
open_points.question: From which clock is the third step's cutoff instant read: the UTC wall clock, the process monotonic clock, or a time captured earlier in the run?
options: Read the UTC wall clock once when the third step starts.
Reuse the run-start or scheduling clock reading.
open_points.default_guess: Read the UTC wall clock exactly once at the start of the third step, because persisted backup instants are UTC wall-clock instants.

witness.initial: A process has remained running since a backup was made, and that backup's recorded UTC instant is near the retention boundary.
events: More than 720 hours of monotonic time pass.
The host's wall clock is set backward before the deletion step starts.
The third step computes its cutoff and examines the backup.
outcomes: Using the UTC wall clock keeps the backup because its recorded age is not yet more than 720 hours.
Using monotonic elapsed time deletes the backup because more than 720 hours have elapsed.
witness.observer: The owner listing kept backups after the run.

open_points.subject: A19
open_points.text: nothing in it is executed or evaluated, and a file over the limit is refused before it is read. The limit is counted over the bytes Registry receives, never over a length the request declares: a declared length over the limit is refused before any byte is read; otherwise Registry reads the upload up to one byte more than the limit and refuses it as soon as it holds more than the limit, whatever length was declared or whether one was.
open_points.question: For an oversized upload whose declared length is absent or not over the limit, is it refused before any file byte is read or only after Registry reads the limit plus one byte?
options: Refuse before reading any byte, which requires some independent knowledge of the actual size.
Read up to 52,428,801 bytes and then refuse.
open_points.default_guess: Read at most the limit plus one byte when the declared length does not already prove the upload oversized, then refuse and retain none of those bytes.

witness.initial: The session already holds a valid uploaded file; a new request has no declared length.
events: The owner uploads a stream containing 52,428,801 bytes.
outcomes: The statement that every over-limit file is refused before it is read permits Registry to consume no file bytes.
The byte-counting rule requires Registry to consume 52,428,801 bytes before refusing, while preserving the earlier session file.
witness.observer: The uploading client, which can observe whether the body is consumed, and the Registry host's resource monitoring.

open_points.subject: A21
open_points.text: files_artifacts (A16, A18) — was reviewed. No outcome changed. files_artifacts now names A19 too
open_points.question: Did the reopened files_artifacts review evaluate A19, or was A19 merely added to the reference list without being reviewed?
options: A19 was reviewed as part of files_artifacts and must be included in the parenthetical evidence.
Only A16 and A18 were reviewed, so files_artifacts remains reopened for A19.
open_points.default_guess: Treat A19 as reviewed and correct the evidence to say `files_artifacts (A16, A18, A19)`.

witness.initial: A19 changes the import-file size and byte-processing rules, and files_artifacts now references A19.
events: The 2026-11-11 review records which changed decisions were examined for files_artifacts.
A later checker or reviewer evaluates whether rule 2's reopening was closed.
outcomes: The prose `files_artifacts (A16, A18)` shows that A19 was not reviewed, so the review remains open.
The sentence `files_artifacts now names A19 too` is read as evidence that A19 was reviewed, so the review is closed.
witness.observer: The design reviewer or lint/checking process deciding whether A21 is complete.

open_points.subject: A21
open_points.text: - concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A01, A04, A07, A12, A13, A14, A16, A18; affected: M01, M03, M04, M05, M06, M09, M10, M11, concurrent creates, corrections, publishes, session changes, single-use confirmation values, confirmations bound to no revision, resubmitted forms on records without a revision, creates racing the erasure that removes their request id, re-uploads replacing a confirmed file, concurrent import confirmations, backup snapshots taken while transactions go on, overlapping backup runs
open_points.question: After A15 added concurrent allocation of audit sequence numbers, must the concurrency review be reopened and name A15, M12 and concurrent audit appends, or is that concurrency subject considered fully covered by the existing A14 reference?
options: Reopen concurrency, add A15 and M12 and review the serialization and transaction failure cases.
Treat A14 as sufficient coverage and leave A15 and M12 unnamed.
open_points.default_guess: Reopen the concurrency category and add A15, M12 and concurrent audit-sequence allocation to its evidence.
